segments.source: This review concerns the current US Three Africas whole-bean blend, not Blue Bottle’s bottled cold brew or a Korean 250 g regional pack. The US page describes two Ethiopian components, one washed and one natural, with a Central African coffee. Its 2026 sourcing feature names Rwanda for that component. The complete farms and varieties are not fixed on the product panel, so check the actual delivered bag before assigning an immutable recipe.
segments.context: This review concerns the current US Three Africas whole-bean blend, not Blue Bottle’s bottled cold brew or a Korean 250 g regional pack. The US page describes two Ethiopian components, one washed and one natural, with a Central African coffee. Its 2026 sourcing feature names Rwanda for that component. The complete farms and varieties are not fixed on the product panel, so check the actual delivered bag before assigning an immutable recipe. [1]

segments.source: The listing calls Three Africas medium roast and elsewhere says the components are roasted with a light touch. Those are roaster descriptions, not an independently measured roast color. Its exact distinction from Giant Steps is a fruit-and-citrus target and declared cold-brew role; Giant Steps is the darker cocoa-led option.

Its exact distinction from Giant Steps is a fruit-and-citrus target and declared cold-brew role; Giant Steps is the darker cocoa-led option. [1] [7]

segments.source: Golden raisin, winey blueberry and lemon zest are Blue Bottle’s target notes. A March 2026 independent home account prepared a particular bag as hot filter coffee, while an older owner discussion describes differing fruit impressions. Neither source can tell us what a new US cold-brew batch tastes like after a long immersion.

segments.source: Blue Bottle’s washed and natural Ethiopian components offer a plausible reason for its advertised fruit range, but processing does not guarantee those notes in every cup. Choose a single bag, write down grind, water and steep time, and compare it black before using milk that may mask the fruit you bought it for.

segments.source: The roaster explicitly says this blend has depth and luminosity when cold-brewed, but the product panel’s 27 g to 350 g hot pour-over guide is not a cold-brew recipe. Follow a dedicated immersion method, use coarse grounds and cold water, filter and refrigerate promptly. Record concentrate dilution separately from the steep recipe.

segments.source: If the first cold cup feels flat, do not infer a defective bag from a single steep: water, grind, time and dilution all change the result. Use the same brew vessel and serving dilution when comparing Three Africas with Peet’s Baridi or Big Bang. A hot bloom schedule should not be transplanted into a cold vessel.

segments.context: Buy Baridi Blend for its documented brew role

segments.source: Baridi is the most direct Peet's bean for someone trying to make its café-style cold brew at home: the roaster says it uses this blend in its coffeebars and designed it to stay aromatic when chilled. Its current product panel, however, shows a sold-out warning. Treat it as a useful reference and buy only if the exact whole-bean bag can be confirmed through a legitimate current seller. Start with one whole-bean bag where available and let a repeatable personal brew decide any larger order.

segments.source: What is Peet's Coffee Baridi Blend?
segments.context: name

segments.source: Peet's calls Baridi its medium-roast coffeebar cold-brew blend and offers a whole-bean selection on the US product page. Its attributes list Africa/Arabia and Americas with washed processing, while its longer story describes a selection of East African washed coffees. That mismatch prevents a fixed country recipe claim. The café drink and this dry bean bag are related but distinct products.

segments.source: Which brew method fits Baridi Blend?
segments.context: name

segments.source: Peet's identifies Baridi as a cold-brew coffee and gives a 12-plus-hour broad method description. A separate Peet's café beverage page says its baristas steep freshly ground Baridi for 12 hours. Neither statement supplies a universal home dose or filtration setup, so start from a dedicated cold-brew method and record coffee, water, grind, time, temperature and dilution.
